subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the overall layout of a six-wheeled heavy carrier: a hull with a front cab, a railgun turret mounted on the rear deck with its barrel elevated forward, and four stabilizer legs for support.

Now I'm working out dimensions and placement—roughly 9m long, 3m wide, with wheels at 0.55m radius, and planning how to structure the build with helper functions for boxes and cylinders, joints for wheel spin and turret rotation, and paint/texture choices for panels, metal, glow effects, and decorative emblems. I'm positioning the chassis, wheel axles, and stabilizer pads so everything sits correctly on the ground plane.

Now I'm detailing the hull geometry—the lower deck body, raked cab with angled windscreen, and fenders over the wheel wells, along with the tire cylinder dimensions matching the wheel radius.

Adding wheel rim, hub, lug nuts, and tread details, then setting up the spin joints along the X-axis so the wheels rotate correctly. I'm also planning the turret assembly with yaw and pitch joints mounted on the deck, plus a railgun with paired barrel rails pitched forward over the cab.

Checking the railgun's elevation angle so the barrel tip clears the cab roof -- a 25-degree pitch keeps it above the 2.9 height limit. I'm building the rail components (box rails, glow strips, capacitor drums, coil rings, muzzle brake) inside the pitch joint, then posing the joint around its own X-axis at roughly -22 degrees to angle the barrel upward.

Now working out the stabilizer legs at the four hull corners, with hinge joints angled outward and down, plus hydraulic leg extensions down to ground pads.

I'm also planning the surface details: hazard stripe decals on the stabilizer arms, emblem textures on the cab and hull, stenciled numbers, glowing cab screens, light bars, antennas, ammo boxes, exhaust stacks, and side ladders to add visual richness.

Now I'm setting up the color palette (olive drab hull, dark steel accents, cyan glow for the rail) and a panelled paint helper with rivet and panel-size parameters, then starting concise box/cylinder helper functions to build out the parts efficiently.

Writing helper functions...

I'm planning how cylinders orient along different axes using rotation arrays, mirroring parts across left/right sides, keeping glow effects as plain color strings, and assigning most parts to a chassis bone. I want to keep the whole script lean, around 300 lines, and now I'm working out the wheel placement logic with spin joints positioned per axle and side.

Adding tire and axle geometry, placing a decal plane for a side emblem with "R-6" text, and designing a hazard stripe texture to apply to the stabilizer arm's front face.
